correctness.rationale: Conditional on r refreshed coordinates, direct order-statistic reasoning proves (n-r+2r/n)/(n+r), including r=0,n. Cactus edge-disjoint cycles make the full change count independent Bernoulli. The mixed copula's pushforward density is explicitly strictly decreasing; integration by parts yields a positive moment representation and strict log-convexity. Discrete convexity proves both cycle-length optimizers. Binomial size biasing gives a uniform O(epsilon^2) coefficient error; Le Cam and independent-cycle bounds prove the Poisson and zero/one thresholds. verify.py completed 554 exact rational assertions, including direct order enumeration; finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: The problem measures whether a random MST survives a natural noise operator. The exact law gives all finite change-count probabilities for an infinite graph family. The non-obvious strict log-convexity yields a complete, sharp, unique all-parameter cycle-allocation optimization at fixed graph resources, and the many-cycle Poisson limit specifies an explicit 1/c refresh threshold. These statements are structural and testable beyond a one-off calculation, with no claim of arbitrary-graph generality.
